name_reason: Already compliant: data_fd2_ (game global) + domain ui_menu + descriptor cursor_idx. The descriptor reflects both the data type (an index/counter scalar) and the purpose (active modal-menu cursor). No Ghidra address residue in the name; no domain ID to preserve (it is a single scalar, not a per-id table). Confirmed semantics via xrefs and decompilation: every menu input loop writes 0 at entry then bumps/reads it to track the highlighted item.
purpose: Shared current-selection cursor index for whichever modal menu is currently active (field command, options, settings, shop buy/sell/give, inventory grid, spell selection, party roster / promote / revive, status, save/load slot picker, chapter-intro menus, and a few non-menu borrow sites).
logic_summary: A single global slot reused by every menu input loop. Each loop writes 0 at entry, increments/decrements it on arrow-key scancodes (wrap-around tested signed via JGE/JLE so it behaves as a signed index in the comparisons), and reads it back on Enter/commit to dispatch the chosen item / member / slot. Wrap and page-step bookkeeping is per-loop (e.g. fd2_count_active_menu_items_until_zero writes it back; party-roster loops pair it with data_fd2_ui_menu_scroll_offset). A handful of non-menu sites borrow the slot while no UI menu is open: fd2_execute_ai_item_use stashes an item id in it between inventory-lookup and effect-apply, fd2_handle_tile_event_interaction and fd2_process_battle_drop_entries reuse it as a transient index. No contention because those paths never run with a menu open.
datatype: uint32 (Ghidra: undefined4, 4 bytes; declared uint32 in globals.h and chintro.c; every access is a full dword)
element_semantics: Single scalar uint32. Value = zero-based index of the currently highlighted item within the active modal menu. Valid range depends on the menu (e.g. 0..3 for the 4-way chapter-intro menu, 0..N-1 for the party roster). Compared as a signed int in the cursor-wrap tests.
comment_original_issue: src comment block (chintro.c lines 776-787) is already accurate and concise: identifies it as the shared modal-menu cursor index, mutable, BSS zero-init, accessed as dword. No issue.
